linux_ledger.what: benchmark ledger regenerated on Linux by the unchanged benchmark code (python -m src.cli build-db; python -m src.cli backtest) in a fresh clone; kept as evidence for the cross-platform comparison. It is NOT the ledger of record.

variants.change: features as 32-bit numbers instead of 64-bit
solver stopping rule 1e-4 changed to 1e-5
iteration limit 2000 changed to 100 (the library default)

C_what_could_hide.predicted_class: none: the field is compared exactly
C_what_could_hide.hit_or_miss: none: the fields are compared exactly
C_what_could_hide.class_based_metrics: none: hit rate, balanced hit rate, macro F-score, counts and confusion matrices must be identical
C_what_could_hide.why_log_loss_is_checked_directly: the record holds a probability of 1.46e-16 for a class that occurred; near zero, a probability tolerance alone does not bound log loss, so the metric itself is compared (1e-06)

changes_that_alter_no_probability: iteration limit 2000 changed to 100 (the library default)

changes_that_alter_a_probability_and_are.change: regularisation strength changed by 1 part in 1e12

comparator_semantics.documented: a difference is refused only when it is greater than its tolerance; a difference exactly equal to the tolerance is accepted
comparator_semantics.note: observed where a difference equal to the tolerance exists as a number; where none exists (None) the two nearest representable differences are tested: the one below is accepted, the one above refused

small_changes_tested_together.ML-LOGIT: two changes, each accepted alone, are refused together: the log loss of their group moves by 1.2 times the metric tolerance
small_changes_tested_together.ML-GBT: not constructible: within the row tolerance of 1e-14 no alteration moves a metric by 0.6 of the metric tolerance (smallest probability of a class that occurred: 9.53e-03); many rows together are refused by the mean tolerance instead
